passages.note: Robert Rivas is listed in the Ayes on the 09/11/19 Assembly Floor concurrence vote, which was not near-unanimous; the first name is included because the page lists two members named Rivas.
passages.actor_quote: Quirk-Silva, Reyes, Luz Rivas, Robert Rivas, Rodriguez, Santiago

passages.provision_quote: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase
passages.note: The chaptered text prints the operative statewide rent cap added as Civil Code Section 1947.12, together with the classes of units it exempts.

rows.reasoning: Rivas voted Aye on AB 1482 (2019-2020), the Tenant Protection Act of 2019, whose operative section bars an owner from increasing rent "more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower" on units that carried no cap before. The same section exempts several classes of units, including "Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years" and deed-restricted affordable housing, so the cap stops short of every rental unit: it does not "Expand rent control to cover all rental units communitywide". A statewide cap that reaches units not previously covered extends coverage rather than maintaining the current set, which matches "Strengthen existing rent stabilization and extend coverage to more units".
